I think it’s a very beautiful city. I think of flamenco, above all, and the culture of the people.”
The Spanish champion finished 11th yesterday in the La Rabida sprint: “You’ve got to reinvent yourself! No, I think it was a very technical sprint; it wasn’t so much about leg strength. And as, unfortunately, our sprinter David González had to withdraw, we were told to give it a go, and I managed to get in there. All in all, I’m happy with this result. I think it’s great to practise these finishes too, because they give you skills that can even come in handy for other types of races later on. I reckon today’s going to be more dangerous. It’ll be an easier day, with far more people getting involved. “[Matthew Brennan] is the fastest rider in this Vuelta; he’s already shown that", Coquard's lead-out man Alexis Renard said this morning. "His team is also the strongest, with a superb lead-out for him in the form of Wout van Aert. There’s not much we can do. Today we’ll see what tactics to put in place to go for first place. Two riders from Sevilla have won stages in La Vuelta:
- Antonio Montes, 3 stage wins across the 1935, 1941 and 1945 editions
- Antonio Piedra, 1 stage win in 2012 (Lagos de Covadonga)

Two riders from Sevilla have won stages in La Vuelta:
- Antonio Montes, 3 stage wins across the 1935, 1941 and 1945 editions
- Antonio Piedra, 1 stage win in 2012 (Lagos de Covadonga)

2nd in 2024? “Yes, the video was played in the Whatsapp chat this morning, and then he explained the finish a bit, and then he said: ‘I went too early, and also I launched for the line too early’; and Pavel [Bittner] did a good ride to come around him. So hopefully we can change it this year on the same finish, but it’s good that he knows the course a bit."

“[Matthew Brennan] is the fastest rider in this Vuelta; he’s already shown that", Coquard's lead-out man Alexis Renard said this morning. "His team is also the strongest, with a superb lead-out for him in the form of Wout van Aert. There’s not much we can do. Today we’ll see what tactics to put in place to go for first place. Two riders from Sevilla have won stages in La Vuelta:
- Antonio Montes, 3 stage wins across the 1935, 1941 and 1945 editions
- Antonio Piedra, 1 stage win in 2012 (Lagos de Covadonga)

Two riders from Sevilla have won stages in La Vuelta:
- Antonio Montes, 3 stage wins across the 1935, 1941 and 1945 editions
- Antonio Piedra, 1 stage win in 2012 (Lagos de Covadonga)

Two riders from Sevilla have won stages in La Vuelta:
- Antonio Montes, 3 stage wins across the 1935, 1941 and 1945 editions
- Antonio Piedra, 1 stage win in 2012 (Lagos de Covadonga)

Two riders from Sevilla have won stages in La Vuelta:
- Antonio Montes, 3 stage wins across the 1935, 1941 and 1945 editions
- Antonio Piedra, 1 stage win in 2012 (Lagos de Covadonga)

- Antonio Montes, 3 stage wins across the 1935, 1941 and 1945 editions
- Antonio Piedra, 1 stage win in 2012 (Lagos de Covadonga)
